<!--
A guard on something apaquarto borrows from quarto rather than a bug that
was fixed. In html and docx, quarto writes a float's caption itself, after
the last point a filter can run, as the word, a non-breaking space, the
number, a colon and the caption: "Figure 1: The caption". apacaption.lua
takes that apart into an APA title, "Figure 1" in bold on a line of its own,
and the caption in italics under it. It recognises the caption by that exact
shape. If quarto changes the shape, nothing fails: the caption is left as
quarto wrote it, run together on one line. The expectations below are for
the split, and "Figure 1:" in the output means the shape has changed --- see
"Dependencies on Quarto internals" in ARCHITECTURE.md.

One of each kind of float: quarto's two, and the Illustration apaquarto
declares under crossref.custom.
-->

::: {#fig-shape}
A figure's content.

The figure caption
:::

::: {#tbl-shape}
| A | B |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |

The table caption
:::

::: {#ill-shape}
An illustration's content.

The illustration caption
:::

See @fig-shape, @tbl-shape and @ill-shape.
